learning_outcomes.text: The student is able to predict the operation of a program based on analysis of the C code.
The student visualizes the operation of a program using flow charts.
The student divides the assignment into sub-problems.
The student converts an assignment into an algorithm.
The student makes the right choices for data structures, data types, and the use of functions and parameters.
The student programs the algorithm using C code.
The student applies correct programming methods.
The student verifies the operation of the program against the requirements of the assignment.

syllabus_topics: Simple C programs: constants and variables, operators, simple input and output, control structures, C standard functions, creating own functions
Static data structures: arrays, arrays of strings, multidimensional arrays, structures
Compilation and syntax checking: compilation process, the preprocessor, header files
Practice themes from theory with small programming exercises
Submission of pre-indicated exercises during each lab session

assessment_methods.method: Lab: Submitted exercises during lab sessions

assessment_rules: The course is evaluated based on two activities: a theory exam and a lab exam. If a student achieves a score of less than 7 on one of the evaluation activities, the student can achieve a maximum of 9/20 for the entire course. For resits, only the written exam (100%) and practical exam (100%) count; points from partial evaluation and penalties for late/non-submission of lab assignments do not apply.
bibliography: Deitel & Deitel. C How To Program international editon.
